customManagers.description: Go's version, from go.dev's release list: go.mod's `go` directive and the Dockerfile's GO_VERSION, moved in one PR. nix/go.nix overrides nixpkgs' go_1_NN onto it; renovate-pins.yaml re-pins GO_DIGEST and derives the source hash.

Node's version, from nodejs.org's release list: engines.node (a `>=` floor), the Dockerfile's node tag and every setup-node node-version, moved in one PR. nix/node.nix overrides nixpkgs' nodejs_NN onto it; renovate-pins.yaml re-pins the image digest and derives the source hash.

packageRules.description: go.mod's own `go` directive is bumped by the regex manager below, which moves the Dockerfile's GO_VERSION in the same PR; left on, gomod would bump the directive alone and leave the copy behind. Same for the node and golang images and the setup actions' node-version, which the node and go regex managers own.

The PR that moves the locked nixpkgs. It no longer touches a toolchain version: nix/{go,node,pnpm}.nix override nixpkgs' package onto the declared patch while the two differ, and .github/workflows/renovate-pins.yaml drops the override's hashes from nix/toolchains.json once the lock catches up. After the major gate on purpose — the later rule wins, so this overrides the major-update dashboard gate above, which a nixpkgs revision would otherwise sit behind forever.
pnpm: package.json's packageManager field and the setup action in CI. Splitting them meant two PRs for one upgrade.

A new Go minor is a new nixpkgs line (go_1_NN), so it waits on the dashboard until nixpkgs packages it; nix/go.nix throws on a line it does not have. Patches open straight away — that is the point of sourcing them from go.dev rather than from the lock.

The pnpm rule above lifts the dashboard gate for the whole group; a pnpm major is a new nixpkgs line (pnpm_NN) and has to wait for it like Go's minor. Node needs no rule of its own: its line is the major, which the generic major gate already holds.
